assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new window on the universe: discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector, followed by evidence for the blazar TXS 0506+056, the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 and neutrino emission from the Galactic plane. It is original in concept and execution, and it is a long-standing cosmic-ray-origin question approached with a new instrument class. Impact is broad across astroparticle physics and multi-messenger astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Halzen drove the IceCube concept and the full-scale detector, and Spiering is a founding figure of neutrino telescopy (Baikal and the early ice efforts). Karle is a credible alternative for the AMANDA-to-IceCube technical path. Any prize is necessarily a representative selection from a collaboration of several hundred, and the exact weighting between instrument builders and analysis leaders is not settled by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the key respect: the diffuse flux was seen above 5 sigma in 2013 and confirmed with independent channels and by later data. Source identifications are more recent, and individual source associations are at 3-5 sigma, so the astrophysical interpretation is still developing, but the discovery of the flux itself is secure and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Individual neutrino sources rest on modest significance and remain under study.
The fair allocation among Halzen, Karle, Spiering and others in a very large collaboration is uncertain.
I am relying on my own recollection of the IceCube results and have not verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and now outperform the caesium standard by orders of magnitude. The invention is clear and original and has lasting impact on metrology, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a forthcoming redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated it; Ye led the highest-precision realisations and the associated frequency-comb and spectroscopy tools. A two-person configuration is natural, although others in the ion-clock and Sr-clock community (for example Hall and Hansch tools already recognised in 2005) have overlapping claims to parts of the field.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: multiple independent labs have reproduced and surpassed the performance over about two decades, with stable interpretation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue as the redefinition of the second approaches.
uncertainties: Overlap with single-ion optical clock work could complicate a clean attribution.
Whether the committee considers this metrology rather than a discovery is a question of taste.
Details of priority between Katori and others are recalled, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC in 2012 completed the Standard Model and was a landmark result in a mega-instrument and detector-physics effort. The 2013 prize recognised the theory only, so the experimental observation has not yet been recognised. As a detector physicist I regard the conception of ATLAS and CMS as nobel-grade scientific engineering.
assessment.attribution: The real difficulty is attribution among thousands of collaborators. Jenni (ATLAS conception and early leadership), Virdee (CMS) and Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the discovery) are plausible, with Della Negra (CMS co-founder) an equal alternative. A three-name cap forces a hard and contestable choice, and the statutes' limit on the number of laureates is a real constraint.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: the particle has been measured by two experiments with growing precision for more than a decade, and couplings are consistent with the Standard Model.
uncertainties: Credit allocation within the collaborations is unusually contested.
Whether the committee wishes to honour experimental discovery separately after the 2013 theory prize.
The choice of three among four credited names is partly arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hardware correction of spherical aberration in electron lenses reached sub-angstrom resolution and made atomic-resolution imaging routine across materials physics. This is a genuine instrumentation breakthrough, comparable in kind to earlier recognised instrument prizes, with very wide downstream use in condensed matter and materials research.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio is coherent: Rose provided the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider built the corrector with the Heidelberg and Julich teams, and Urban led the implementation in transmission instruments. Others (Krivanek on STEM correction) could dispute the allocation, and that is a real unresolved issue.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of independent use and replication in commercial instruments. Recognition is timely, though it risks being viewed as chemistry or materials science rather than physics.
uncertainties: Krivanek and the STEM-corrector line of work may have an equally strong claim.
Boundary with chemistry/materials science may count against it for a physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators, providing the readout and control architecture of most superconducting quantum processors. It has had large and lasting influence on quantum technology and fundamental tests of light-matter interaction.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf form a natural triplet: the 2004 proposal (Blais with Huang, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff with Schoelkopf's group). Girvin and the Yale team are also central, so the allocation is not entirely clear. The 2025 prize on superconducting circuits already recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling, which both helps (field is validated) and complicates (overlap) the case.
assessment.maturity: Mature in science: reproduced in many labs for twenty years. Timing is plausible, but the committee may prefer to let the 2025 recognition settle before honouring a closely related area.
uncertainties: Allocation with Girvin, Devoret and others is contestable.
Overlap with the most recent circuit-related prize could weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter, with an enormous follow-on literature including fractional Chern states.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery with Cao and Fatemi as principal co-workers. The trio is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration, though the early student authors and other groups complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Intermediate maturity: key results have been replicated by several groups, but the nature of the superconducting state and the correlated insulators is still debated. Recognition may be slightly early relative to the stabilisation of the interpretation.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unsettled.
Credit for the experimental side to junior authors and to Kim and other groups is not fully clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Event Horizon Telescope images of the M87 and Sgr A* shadows are direct, striking observations of strong-field gravity near horizons, building on the earlier Nobel recognition of black-hole theory and the Galactic centre. The technical achievement of global millimetre VLBI is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Falcke provided the shadow concept for imaging and Doeleman led the VLBI realisation; Narayan contributed the key theoretical modelling. A tight prize would need to decide between idea, instrument and theory, and the collaboration is large.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: M87 and Sgr A* images are consistent with each other and with general relativity, but independent confirmation by a different array is lacking and polarisation and jet interpretations are ongoing.
uncertainties: No independent array has reproduced the images.
Weighting of Narayan against Falcke and Doeleman is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors enabled precision vertexing and tracking in modern collider experiments and, in time, medical and photon-science imaging. The Charpak prize precedent shows that detector inventions can be recognised, and these devices were essential for heavy-flavour physics and the Higgs programme.
assessment.attribution: Parker (planar and 3D silicon concepts), Heijne and Jarron (hybrid pixels at CERN) are plausible, but the credit is spread over several developers (Kemmer, Hyams, Rancoita and others), so the three credited names may not be the decisive ones.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of ubiquitous use and independent replication. Timing is acceptable, but the long history makes the identification of unique originators difficult.
uncertainties: Priority among silicon-detector pioneers is contested and my knowledge is incomplete.
The committee may consider this an enabling technology rather than a discovery.
